newsitem.title: USA: New life insurance sales rules proposed in N.Y..
newsitem.headline: New life insurance sales rules proposed in N.Y..

text.p: The New York insurance department proposed new rules to protect consumers from the inappropriate replacement of life insurance policies and annuities, a practice known as churning or twisting.
The new rules relate both to the conduct of life insurance agents and insurance companies when an existing policy is replaced with a new one.
The proposed regulation would provide customers with more information and creates a cooling-off period in which policyholders could reverse transactions, the insurance department said.
A public hearing on the proposal was scheduled for 1000 EDT/1400 GMT September 17 at the insurance department's New York City office and comment from interested parties was requested.
"Inappropriate replacement of a consumer's existing life insurance coverage continues to be a serious problem," said Superintendent of Insurance Edward Muhl.

"Our regulation puts the onus squarely on the agent and the insurance company to know exactly what coverage a prospective client has and how the replacement transaction will affect that existing coverage," he said in a statement.
"This includes borrowing from the cash build-up of the coverage to pay for the replacement policy," he said.

He said the department will require both the agent and the company to keep detailed information on such transactions including sales illustrations, so that the department will be able to review this data during market conduct examinations.
The new regulation would require agents to obtain with each application a complete list of all the applicant's existing life insurance policies or annuities.
If a new transaction involves replacement of an existing policy, then a disclosure statement must be completed.
Insurers also must designate a senior corporate officer to be responsible for monitoring and enforcing these rules.
